Separating the two lets us first identify whether a practice is punishment, then ask whether it is justified. If the definition already builds in a justification such as "deserved suffering," debates about deterrence or rehabilitation become definitional disputes, and practices get called punishment before anyone has shown them to be defensible. Punishment also exists as a social institution whatever reasons are offered for it, so we should describe it as it is before judging the reasons.

CONFIDENCE: 85
